resale_co.name: Certificate of Title Transfer (zoning and flood conformance inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Office of Code Enforcement, Zoning Officer (Zoning Official / Flood Plain Administrator)
resale_co.contact_title: Zoning Official/Code Officer/Community Development Director (signs the title transfer certificate)
resale_co.valid_for: 180 days after issuance, for one transfer only (Code Section 214-7)
requirements: Zoning conformance inspection: the structure or unit must comply with Chapter 560, Zoning
Flood conformance inspection against the required design flood elevation (DFE + 2 or 11 feet), with the assessed value of the structure recorded
Inspector enters with the realtor's key; if no realtor or manager is listed, the owner must set an appointment during the inspection week
Not required for transfers of new construction when the original certificate of occupancy was issued within 18 months of the transfer
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Certificate of Title Transfer (property address, block and lot, seller, purchaser, agent, scheduled closing date) and submit it with payment (check or cash) to the Office of Code Enforcement, Borough Hall, 9508 Second Avenue, Stone Harbor, NJ 08247 (609-368-6814, MSTEICH@SHNJ.ORG). Listing a realtor lets the official use the realtor's key. Office open to the public Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.

evidence.quote: No person, persons or organization of persons shall sell or transfer title to any structure, portion of structure or unit
Applications for a certificate of title transfer shall be submitted to the Zoning Officer of the Borough of Stone Harbor
A certificate of title transfer shall be valid for a period of 180 days after issuance
A certificate of title transfer is not required for transfers of new construction,
The fee for a certificate of title transfer shall be $50 per unit
APPLICATION FOR CERTIFICATE OF TITLE TRANSFER THE BOROUGH OF STONE HARBOR OFFICE OF CODE ENFORCEMENT
ZONING FEE: $50.00 FLOOD INSPECTION FEE: $50.00 TOTAL DUE: $100.00
Zoning Official/Code Officer/ Community Development Director Matthew Steich

resale_co.notes: Borough Code Chapter 214 (Certificate of Title Transfer, read in full through the ecode360 print view) bars selling or transferring title to any structure or unit without a certificate of title transfer from the Zoning Officer, who inspects for compliance with Chapter 560, Zoning. The certificate is good for 180 days and one transfer. New construction is exempt when the original CO was issued within 18 months of the transfer. Violations carry a fine of not less than $100 (Section 214-8). The code sets the fee at $50 per unit, which matches the zoning fee on the form; the form adds a $50 flood inspection fee, for $100 total. In October 2026 the Construction page started linking a re-posted copy of the April 2023 form (Cert-of-title-transfer.pdf, a scan) that names Matt Steich, Zoning Official, and MSTEICH@SHNJ.ORG instead of Ray Poudrier; fees are unchanged. The older text copy of the form (2023/04 upload) is still online and shows the same fees. Rick Allen is Construction Official, Building/Mechanical Sub-code Official and Flood Plain Administrator (AllenR@shnj.org). Stone Harbor also runs a rental license and rental fire inspection program through the Fire Prevention Bureau (single family: rental license $200 plus fire inspection $100); that is for rentals only, not sales.

requirements: On-site inspection by the Stone Harbor Bureau of Fire Prevention; closing or leasing before the certificate is issued carries a $500.00 penalty
Smoke alarms over ten years old must be replaced; battery alarms must be 10-year sealed battery type; wired alarms may not be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke alarm type and number depend on the year built or renovated (for example, homes from March 1991 on need wired, interconnected alarms on all levels and inside each sleeping room)

CO alarms on sleeping levels within 10 feet of every bedroom door when there is an attached garage, fuel-burning appliance or fireplace; CO alarms not more than 10 years old; homes built 2015 or later need hard-wired CO alarms
Low-voltage fire alarm systems must be tested by a NJ licensed alarm contractor with an NFPA 72 report sent to the Bureau

Form (October 2022) still requires a fire extinguisher: minimum 2A:40BC, not over 10 pounds, in or within 10 feet of the kitchen on its bracket, top no more than 5 feet up, serviced within the past year or bought within 6 months with receipt, manual left for the buyer
All open construction permits must be closed before settlement

fire_cert.notes: NJ DCA lists Stone Harbor's fire code enforcing agency as its fire department (F). The Borough's Fire Prevention Bureau page (live, October 2026) names Acting Fire Official Mike Gihorski; a December 2025 archive copy named Fire Official Roger W. Stanford at (609) 368-5102 Ext 709. The Bureau page hides email addresses, so the email shown is from the NJ DCA fire directory (survey 3/6/2025). The application is dated October 2022 and still requires a fire extinguisher despite P.L.2025, c.19; confirm with the Bureau. Three-unit and larger tiers ($80.00, $130.00, $185.00, plus $15.00 per unit over 3) are on the form but not listed above because they do not apply to 1-2 family homes. Closing or leasing before the certificate is issued carries a $500.00 penalty (shown on the form; listed under requirements, not as a fee).
